title: Token boundary normalizer + chat-schema fallback for onboarding pipelines
creator: Aditi Rao
description: New onboarding runs occasionally produce misaligned token counts and malformed chat frames for certain open models (notably 3rd-party forks with atypical role delimiters). This ticket implements a token boundary normalizer and a chat-schema fallback layer in the onboarding pipeline so that: 1) uploaded model bundles are validated for delimiter/tokenization incompatibilities, 2) we can emit a compatibility shim when minor divergence is detected, and 3) performance profiles are only published after normalization checks pass.
reproduction_steps: 1) Upload model bundle `community/gptx-fork-v0.9` to staging onboarding pipeline
2) Run onboarding pin job with default chat template 'assistant:;user:'
3) Observe tokenization mismatch telemetry: role separators split into extra subtokens and prefix trimming changes generation length
4) Run inference smoke test with canonical chat examples -> see message framing errors and token miscount in runtime traces
root_cause_summary: Certain community model distributions replace conventional role delimiters (e.g. '\n<|user|>') with compact or multi-byte delimiters. Our existing onboarding checks only compare raw token counts against benchmarks and do not normalize delimiter variants, leading to profile pollution and downstream latency/cost misestimates.
proposed_solution: Implement Token Boundary Normalizer (TBN): canonicalize common role delimiter variants into a normalized token sequence during onboarding tokenization checks
Add Chat-Schema Fallback: when TBN detects >5% divergence in role tokenization, generate a per-model shim that translates incoming chat frames to the model's native delimiter before serving
Tighten publish gating: only publish performance profile if normalized rollout smoke tests pass and regression delta < 3% for token counts and latency
Emit structured telemetry for each normalization decision so we can audit shim frequency and measure customer impact
implementation_plan: A. Library: add tbn module to onboarding service (Python) with a configurable delimiter map and heuristic fallbacks
B. Pipeline: wire TBN into tokenization-phase of onboarding jobs and compute normalized token distributions
C. Shim artifacts: produce a small JSON shim (role_map + escape_rules) stored with the model bundle and surfaced in the model catalog
D. Runtime: update serving runtime to apply shim at request ingress for pinned models (opt-in until stable), with a flag to disable for Dedicated/Private deployments
E. Tests: unit tests for 12 delimiter variants + end-to-end smoke on staging and canary on 10% of new onboarding runs
F. Telemetry: add metrics 'tbn.applied', 'tbn.divergence_pct', 'tbn.shim_created' and dashboard in Console
acceptance_criteria: Onboarding runs with known delimiter variants produce a normalized token count that aligns within 3% of canonical baseline
For models that require a shim, a shim JSON is recorded in the bundle and serving runtime applies the shim in canary with no message corruption
Performance profile publication is blocked when TBN reports an unresolved divergence (>10%) and an explicit manual review flag is set
Dashboard shows TBN metrics and incidence rate; stakeholders can query list of shims created in past 30 days
progress_updates: 2026-03-02: Spike completed — gathered 14 community models with delimiter abnormalities and produced sample tokenization diffs (Aditi)
2026-03-04: PoC TBN module implemented; handles ascii and utf-8 multibyte delimiters; unit tests added for 8 patterns (Marcus)
2026-03-06: Integrated TBN into onboarding job runner; initial runs show shim creation for 3/14 models, divergence_pct ~ 6-12% (Aditi)
2026-03-08: Design review with PM/Console team — decided to store shim as metadata alongside model bundle and surface in catalog UI (Design: Priya Sengupta)
2026-03-10: Began runtime canary: pushing shim-enabled handling to 2 serving nodes behind canary flag; no observed message corruption in 48h so far (Marcus)
blockers: Need runtime approval for applying shims by default in Hosted API (open: security review for input rewriting)
Edge case: some model families intentionally rely on delimiter byte sequences for steering; risk of changing behavior if shim applied incorrectly
decisions: Store shim as immutable JSON artifact attached to model bundle instead of patching model weights
Canary runtime application will be opt-in until 2026-03-17 after 5 full days of no regressions
If divergence > 10% then onboarding will mark model as 'manual-review' and block profile publish

Add catalog UI row for 'Shim present' and link to shim details (owner: Priya)
